system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived

    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    The promotional test grew paid conversions by 31% and monthly revenue by 18% in the low-touch segment, although the observation window was 12 weeks; the support model was the same throughout.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two measured deficits this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage single slot is the one that attacks the funnel stage that actually regressed rather than the one that answers the competitor's price move emotionally. memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) maps directly onto both symptoms, and it is reinforced by memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifted first-week activation) and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging lifted week-one engagement); three independent-looking records pointing the same direction is a stronger base than any single one. I chose onboarding over activation_messaging because onboarding sits upstream and its improvement should propagate into activation, whereas messaging alone cannot fix a flow people are abandoning. I want memory_86 verified precisely because I am leaning on it: I need to know whether the lift was in completion rate only or in downstream retained revenue, and whether the tested population resembles today's price-pressured SMB cohort. I want memory_73 verified even though I am not choosing it, because it is the loudest counter-pull in the room: a 31%/18% promotional result is exactly the memory that will be invoked to justify matching the competitor's entry pricing, and its own record flags the two things that would undermine it — a 12-week observation window and an unchanged support model. A 12-week window cannot distinguish durable revenue from pulled-forward or discount-attracted revenue that churns in months 4-6, and an unchanged support model means the result may not survive the volume it would create. If the archive shows no retention tail, memory_73 should be downgraded as evidence for sustainable qualified revenue, not treated as a proven play. I am not verifying memory_57 or memory_44 because neither addresses the regressed stage: referrals act on established customers and enterprise sales-assist acts on a different segment entirely. Downstream value risk is real even for my chosen action — stripping onboarding steps can raise completion while admitting less-qualified accounts, so success must be measured on retained qualified revenue at 8-12 weeks, not on completion rate alone, and I will keep a qualification checkpoint intact rather than removing every field. Standard experiment scale with a holdout; the inherited evidence is suggestive and directionally consistent but not yet confirmed on the revenue metric that actually matters, so I want a clean read rather than a broad commitment.
